guide.title: DIY Rainwater Harvesting System Installation
steps:
**Step 1: Planning & Assessment**
- Calculate roof catchment area (length × width)
- Determine annual rainfall in your area
- Estimate water harvesting potential: Area (m²) × Rainfall (mm) × 0.8 (efficiency)
- Choose appropriate tank size based on needs and space

**Step 2: Gutter Installation**
- Install gutters along roof edges with 1-2° slope toward downspout
- Ensure gutters are clean and free from debris
- Secure gutters every 1-1.5 meters with brackets
- Seal all joints to prevent leakage

**Step 3: First Flush System**
- Install first flush diverter near the downspout
- This diverts the initial dirty water (first 5mm of rain)
- Use a 4" PVC pipe as diverter chamber
- Install a small ball valve at the bottom for cleaning

**Step 4: Filtration Setup**
- Install mesh screen/leaf guard at gutter entry points
- Add second-stage filter before tank inlet
- Use 1-2mm mesh for effective filtration
- Ensure easy access for periodic cleaning

**Step 5: Tank Installation**
- Place tank on stable, level platform (elevated if possible)
- Keep away from direct sunlight (use covered area)
- Install inlet pipe at top with mosquito mesh
- Install overflow pipe near the top of the tank
- Add outlet tap/valve at bottom (10cm from base)

**Step 6: Pipe Connections**
- Connect downspout to first flush diverter
- Connect diverter outlet to filter system
- Connect filtered water line to tank inlet
- Install overflow pipe directing excess water to drainage or garden
- Use appropriate slopes (minimum 1:100) for gravity flow

**Step 7: Tank Preparation**
- Clean tank thoroughly before first use
- Cover tank top with tight-fitting lid
- Ensure all openings have mosquito mesh
- Mark water level indicator on tank exterior

**Step 8: Testing & Commissioning**
- Test system with water hose before first rain
- Check all connections for leaks
- Verify first flush diverter operation
- Ensure overflow functions correctly
- Clean gutters and filters

**Step 9: Maintenance Schedule**
- **Weekly (monsoon season)**: Check gutters and filters
- **Monthly**: Clean first flush system, inspect pipes
- **Quarterly**: Deep clean filters, check tank water quality
- **Annually**: Full system inspection, tank cleaning, seal check

**Step 10: Water Treatment (Optional)**
- For potable use: Add chlorine tablets or install UV filter
- For gardening: Use as-is after basic filtration
- For household use (non-potable): Ensure proper filtration
- Test water quality periodically
materials_needed: Basic tools: hacksaw, measuring tape, drill, spirit level

cost_saving_tips: Buy materials during off-season (summer) for better prices
Consider used/recycled tanks if in good condition
Group purchase with neighbors for bulk discounts
Start with basic system, upgrade gradually
common_mistakes: Not installing first flush - leads to tank contamination
Insufficient slope in pipes - causes water stagnation
Undersized gutters - overflow during heavy rain
No mosquito mesh - breeding ground for mosquitoes
Tank in direct sunlight - promotes algae growth
safety_tips: Work with partner when on roof
Use proper ladder and safety harness
Turn off electricity in work area
Wear gloves when handling PVC adhesive
Ensure tank platform can support full weight (1L = 1kg)
optimization_tips: Paint tank white to reflect heat
Add multiple taps at different heights
Install water level indicator for monitoring
Use diversion valve to switch between storage and drainage
Connect multiple tanks in series for larger capacity
